name: Basilika Wilten
kurzbeschreibung: The Basilika Wilten in Innsbruck is considered one of Austria's most magnificent Rococo churches, featuring delicate stucco work and a rich pilgrimage history.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Basilika Wilten ? officially the Pfarr- und Wallfahrtskirche Unserer Lieben Frau unter den vier S?ulen ? is a Baroque and early Neoclassical jewel on the southern outskirts of the Tyrolean state capital, Innsbruck. Rising in immediate proximity to the historic Stift Wilten, it ranks among the most architecturally accomplished Rococo church buildings in the entire Alpine region. Owing to its supra-regional significance in ecclesiastical history, it was elevated to the rank of a papal Basilica minor by Pope Pius XII in 1957. As the historic mother parish of Innsbruck, this sacred site boasts an uninterrupted spiritual tradition reaching back to late Roman antiquity.

History & Architecture

Archaeological excavations prove that an early Christian hall church belonging to the ancient Roman fort of Veldidena already stood on this site in the 5th century. From 1140 onwards, the Premonstratensian canons of Stift Wilten assumed pastoral care. A Marian pilgrimage has been documented since 1259; at the heart of veneration to this day stands the late Gothic sandstone statue Maria unter den vier S?ulen (dating to c. 1320?1380) beneath an ornate canopy. The present church building was erected between 1751 and 1756 according to designs by master builder Joseph Stapf of Pfronten. Construction supervision was entrusted to the Wilten parish priest and gifted priest-architect Franz de Paula Penz. Master craftsmen of the highest caliber designed the interior: Wessobrunn plasterer Franz Xaver Feuchtmayer and Anton Gigl created buoyant rocailles in soft pink, white, and gold, while Augsburg court painter Matth?us G?nther created monumental ceiling frescoes depicting the life of the Virgin Mary. In 1988, Pope John Paul II visited the basilica.

Visit & Getting There

The Basilika Wilten is open daily throughout the year from 07:30 to 18:00 (sightseeing visits are not permitted during church services). Admission to the sanctuary is free of charge; donations for the preservation of this sacred monument are welcome. Group guided tours can be arranged through the parish office of Wilten. Arrival by public transport: From Innsbruck city centre, tram line 1 runs directly to the Bergisel stop (approx. a 3-minute walk to the church); alternatively, visitors can reach the forecourt via tram line 6, the Stubaitalbahn (STB) to the Stift Wilten stop, or the tourist Sightseer bus line. By car: Via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Innsbruck-Mitte/Wilten) or the Brennerautobahn A13 (exit Innsbruck-S?d); pay parking is available along Bergiselweg and around the monastery.

Tips

Via the paved church square, there is a lateral, step-free entrance that provides barrier-free access for wheelchair users and visitors with strollers; the interior of the church is entirely level. Be sure to combine your visit with a tour of the adjacent Stift Wilten, with its collegiate church and Baroque museum. A special artistic highlight are the festive Sunday masses, featuring high-caliber choirs and orchestras performing classical sacred music.
